request_context: A request to turn an approved feature requirements document and design into an ordered list of implementation tasks for a coding agent to execute.

rules.source_quote: every task must link to at least one requirement
rules.outcome: Each task says which requirement or requirements it serves.
rules.why: Reviewers can trace every piece of work back to a need and spot work nobody asked for.
rules.scenario_hint: Requirements document with many numbered items and a design that adds extra components.

rules.source_quote: Requirement references: `_Requirements: X.Y_` linking back to requirements.md
rules.outcome: Requirement links sit in the same place and look the same in every task.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to produce an implementation task list.

rules.source_quote: Tasks are ONLY coding tasks — no deployment, documentation, or user testing
rules.outcome: The plan contains only work that is done by writing or changing code; deployment, writing documentation and manual user testing are left out.
rules.why: Every item can be handed to a coding agent and finished without human steps.
rules.scenario_hint: Feature spec mentions a rollout, user docs or a pilot with real users.

rules.source_quote: Each task builds incrementally on previous tasks
rules.outcome: Each task builds on earlier ones, and no task depends on something that comes after it.
rules.why: The list can be executed top to bottom without getting stuck.

rules.source_quote: Order tasks by dependency (foundation → core → polish)
rules.outcome: Shared structure and interfaces come first, the main feature logic next, and error handling and edge cases last.
rules.why: A working main path exists early and hardening builds on it.
rules.scenario_hint: Design that includes validation, error cases and a core data model.

rules.source_quote: Map each requirement to implementation tasks
rules.outcome: Every requirement in the input is covered by at least one task; none is silently dropped.
rules.why: Coverage gaps show up in the plan instead of during testing.
rules.scenario_hint: Requirements include easily overlooked items such as error handling or permissions.

rules.source_quote: Tasks too large (should be completable by an LLM in one pass)
rules.outcome: Each task is small enough to be implemented and checked in a single focused pass.
rules.why: Large tasks make automated execution unreliable and hard to review.
rules.scenario_hint: Large feature that tempts a plan with a few huge steps.

rules.outcome: Each task has a clear objective plus specific details on what to create or change.
rules.why: The executor knows what 'done' looks like.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to produce an implementation task list.

rules.source_quote: Numbered checkbox list: `- [ ] N.` for top-level, `- [ ] N.M` for sub-tasks
rules.outcome: Tasks are numbered and each has a checkbox that can be ticked off.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to produce an implementation task list.

rules.source_quote: Max 2 levels of hierarchy (top-level + one sub-level)
rules.outcome: The plan nests at most two levels: top-level tasks with sub-tasks beneath them.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to produce an implementation task list.

rules.source_quote: Sub-tasks indented 2 spaces under their parent
rules.outcome: Sub-tasks are visibly nested beneath their parent task.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to produce an implementation task list.

rules.outcome: The plan is saved to the location the request names for the feature's spec files and nowhere else.
rules.why: Teammates and tooling look for the plan in one agreed place.
rules.scenario_hint: Request names a folder where the feature's requirements and design already live.
